By: Carol Albertyn Christie | Production

Proposal


Show:

Further information:
Vervet Monkey Proposal

Tracy Rowls runs a rehab centre for vervet monkeys along the South Coast of KZN. It is called Umsizi Umkomaas Rehan Centre. For the past 16 years she had taken monkeys in and either acted as a foster parent for the young monkeys or helped monkeys that have been injured.
There is an uneasy tension with monkeys along the KZN. Due to urbanization vervets have lost their habitat and live alongside humans. There is the one camp that see vervets as a nuisance and the others who believe we should try and live in harmony.

Vervets have become habituated and are a nuisance when they come into homes and ransack kitchens. They will pull vegetables out of the ground and eat unripe fruit. At schools they also feed on the high calorie food that children leave behind. They can be aggressive.

Some people actively dissuade vervets through srapying water on them or shooting them with pellet guns.

The vet at Riverside says that almost 90% of monkeys that she sees has pellets lodged in their bodies when she X Rays them.

Locals call Tracy the monkey lady and she is always there to help primates in distress. She lives in a suburban area and until recently had 119 monkeys on her property.

Her neighbours were understandably unhappy about the amount of monkeys that she had. Tracy does not have a permit to house monkeys. Although she has applied to Ezemvelo several times they have not granted her a permit.

In February Ezemvelo told her to find a place for the monkeys or they would confiscate them.

Tracy has been for some time trying to find land to move the monkeys to. Her hope is to consolidate the monkeys into tribes and release them into the wild.

(The jury is out as to whether monkeys can survive in the wild when they have been habituated. Whether without learning from adults they would know what food to eat.)

Tracy did not find land and Ezemvelo came one Saturday morning and confiscated over 50 of her monkeys.
CROW, another wild life rehab centre helped them catch the monkeys.
What no-one knew was that Ezemvelo had no intention of releasing these monkeys into the wild and they were driven in a truck and euthenised.

On inspection some of the cages that Tracy had kept the monkeys in were in a bad state. She obviously lacks the funds to look after them and the cages had rusty nails sticking out of the wood.

The SPCA was also there to monitor the capture of the monkeys and they too did not know that the monkeys would be killed.

Tracy has taken out a court order against Ezemvelo taking any more monkeys and the case will be heard on the 19th of May.

Vervets are not endangered. But what line does one draw?
Rehabbing vervets is very expensive and time consuming and academics argue that the money used to help monkeys could be better spent on other conservation initiatives.

Vervets Script 18 plus promos

Primate Paramedics

V/O (JUST MY SUGGESTIONS)
Hardly a day passes without vervet monkeys killed or injured along the KwazuluNatal East Coast. Volunteer organisations like Monkey Helpline and Umsizi Umkomaas Rehabilitation Centre make it their mission to act as primate paramedics.


Up Sound
“This monkey looks like he is in a bad way.”

V/O
Steve Smit and Carol Booth from Monkey Helpline have been called out to help a monkey that was mauled by a dog and had been cowering covered in blood behind a house.
This couple have dedicated their lives to rescueing and rehabilitating injured monkeys. Their service is free and operates 24/7.
(or and they operate 24/7/365 full time?)

Steve
“So you phone us and I have a monkey lying on the ground her, I have a monkey sitting with it’s arm hanging off. Or it’s inside are hanging out. But we try to get someone there who will acess the animal. Then we will go out there and rescue it.

V/O
Carol and Steve rescue about 100 monkeys every month. Saldy they say up to 75% die due to the severity of their injuries. They have about 250 monkeys here at their rehabilitation centre in Camperdown that they have personally rescued.

Carol
“Whether you like monkeys or not, whether you care whether they get rehabilitated or not, you cannot leave a monkey to suffer on the side of a road or in a garden leave it there and just walk away. Somebody has to respond.

V/O
They’re classified as of “least concern” on the endangered list, but with urbanisation comes busy streets, dogs, electric fences and humans. Numbers are dwindling .

Dr Kerry Easson is known as the monkey vet in Durban – she feels humans are the invaders.

Kerry
“You know I walways say there are no monkey problems there are people’s problems, it’s a tolerance issue. So you will get one neighbour who is happy with them and the other who does not tolerate them and throws rocks and shooting at them. The pellet shooting is a massive, massive problem.”

V/O
Alarmingly almost every monkey that Dr Easson sees has pellets embedded in ITS body.

Kerry
‘There is the pellet and you can actually see it has actually shattered the spine and you can see the shrapnel from the pellet.”

V/O
Realising the growing need to care for injured or orphaned vervets, Tracy Rowles started the Umsizi Vervet Rescue Centre down the South Coast. She’s dedicated 17 years of her life to monkey rescue.

Up Sound Hey Sweetie

Link
This group of monkeys behind me for a few months now. It is hoped that they will form a tight troop and be able to be released into the wild. Tracy Rowles believes that they are not pets and they should and deserve to be free.

V/O
It’s breaks her heart to lose a life, but reuniting healed monkeys with family groups makes it all worthwhile for Rowles. A video of one of her primate’s being released was viewed over 20 million times.

Tracy
“It makes everything and all the hard work worthwhile. It’s an amazing feeling to see them back with their troop and family.“

V/O
But this good news story soon turned into a nightmare for Rowles when a neighbour complained about the monkeys being kept in an urban area and alerted the authorties.

Tracy
“We were in the process every morning of preparing food and starting to clean cages. I saw motor vehicles pulling up all along our road, saw a big truck and I started coming down the driveway to see what was going on.”

V/O (there’s also an Ezemvelo nature reserve – so I would, for clarity keep referring to KZN Wildlife as well otherwise it’s confusing for anyone not from KZN)
Ezemvelo KZN Wildlife arranged various animal wellfare organisations and the municilaity, to come and help them capture and confiscate the monkeys that Rowles was looking after.

Tracy
“And I tried to close my door telling him he couldn’t come in without a warrant and trying to get hold of my attorneys and they just pushed the door in and came in like ants.”

V/O
KZN Wildlife’s reason for confiscating the monk eys was that Rowles was unable to look after them in an urban area and that she was not licenced to look after indigenous primates.

Tracy
“I was told I had to go to the police station. I had to sign a form of guilt for not having a permit. We then came back and I sat in the driveway cause I couldn’t bear the sounds of listening to all of the monkeys screaming in stress and fear.

V/O
What Tracy Rowles did not know at the time, was that Ezemvelo KZN Wildlife would take the healthy monkeys away and euthanise them all.

Tashya
“And then they were taken and driven out and murdered and I will ephatically say they were murdered at Umfolosi Game Reserve.”

V/O
Rowles called in her attorney, Tashya Giyapersad who argued that it was unlawful for Dr Jones to enter the property by force, since she’s applied for three separate permits on behalf of Umsizi since 2018.

Up sound

Tashya
“To date we have not heard of a refusal for those permits.”

Masa
‘At the time that you did this you thought that this was the right body to apply for a permit with?”

Tashya
“It was the only body to apply for a permit. They will then write to you we would now refer the matter to the MEC and the MEC will grant you an exemption and we give you consent. But this did not happen here.”

V/O
Ezemvelo KZN WILDLIFE is governed by the Nature Conservation Ordinance 15 of 1974. Nearly 50 years ago, vervets were REGARDED as vermin and policy makers did not anticipate the need for regulating rehabilitation and rescue centres.



Steve
“The ordinance is an out dated document from 1974, Ordinance 15 and in that Ordinance it states that nobody is allowed to get a permit for a monkey or baboon from KZN Wildlife.

V/O
But the body can grant permits to circuses, zoos or research institutes that perform scientific tests on monkeys. Only the MEC can give Ezemvelo KZN WILDLIFE a concession to grant the permit.


Tashya
“Now we need to recognise that primates are sentient beings, they are not just property, they are not some group or species that needs to be rounded up and killed. So while we may have an idea for a protection of a domestic dog or cat , there is not the same for vervets.”

V/O CARON
To address the rights of vervets, the national SPCA’s Karen Trendler – together with other organisations – developed the Norms and Standards for the Management of Primates in 2008 – it was meant to replace the old ordinance.

Karen (Caron not karen)
“It would help from both a conservation permiting and welfare compliance point of view if that structure was in place. So that you had very set guidelines to what you can and can’t do.”

V/O Trendler says it was up to Ezemvelo Wildlife to adopt the new guidelines. While it periodically inspected Umsizi, Ezemvelo confiscated the vervets in March this year because Umsizi still didn’t have a permit in terms of the old framework.

Masa
“So you are given 21 days to get rid of how many monkeys?

Tracy
“We are told to get rid of 117 monkeys in 21 days and there was no where for them to go there is no facility that would be able to take that amount of monkeys.”

Up sound

V/O
As promised on the 29th of March Ezemvelo took about half of Umsizi’s 117 monkeys. The person heading up the confiscation WAS Dr Roy Jones, a senior district conservation manager at Ezemvelo. He did not tell Umsizi what he was going to do with the monkeys, but in his court affidavit he STATED that they had all been all euthanised.


V/O
Ezemvelo asked South Africa’s oldest rehabilitation Centre, CROW in Durban, to assist them catching the monkeys on the day.

Clint Halkett-Siddall is Crow’s Operational Manager and says Ezemvelo told him the monkeys would be taken to Zululand.

Masa
“Now when you heard that these monkeys actually weren’t taken to Zululand and you found out what happened what were your thoughts?”
(Cut out)

Clive
“We were obviously devastated as a team you know, we try to make sure that any animal is able to have a life back in the wild again.We actually took a decision with exco going forward that if Ezemvelo asked us for something like this we would say no.”

V/O
He says that CROW offered to house the Umsizi monkeys that Ezemvelo confiscated, but Ezemvelo turned down CROW’s offer on the day.

Masa
“So right now they could be here?”

Clint
“Any animals that could have been rehabilitated could have been here.We would have tried to get them to a point of release as soon as possible.”

Masa
“And instead?”

Clint
“Um ja.”

V/O
Ezemvelo has no rehabilitation centres of their own. In Jones’ affidavit he said that the monkeys “ could not be placed in any licensed rehabilitation centre.” Monkey Helpline disagrees.

Steve
If we had been asked by Ezemvelo at the time if we could have accomodated the monkeys from Tracy’s place the answer would have been emphatically yes. We have got the space and we would have built the cages and we would never have allowed them to be taken off into the fate that they were ultimately subjected to.




Link
“These are the Ezemvelo KZN Wildlife Head Offices in Pietermaritzburg. They are responsible for confiscating the vervet monkeys in March this year. We’ve requested an interview with them to get some answers, but they have declined the interview.”

V/O
We PHONED Dr Roy Jones who HAD headed up the operation.

Roy
“Roy Jones good day.”

Masa
“Good day Dr Jones this is Masa Kekana from CB.”

Roy
“Our CEO has already advised Carte Blanche that we are not in a position to discuss this at this stage.”

Masa
“But you were the ones who captured the monkeys?”

Roy
“No, not personally no.”

Masa
“Your organisation initiated this?”

Roy
“We initiated it, but we weren’t directly involved in the capture.”

Masa
“But you were there?”

Roy
“Correct”

Masa
“So you were involved and you are fully aware?”

Roy
“Yes, no, I am , I was just answering the question that you posed to me and I was just correcting it.”

V/O EZEMVELO FACEBOOK TITLE
It remains a mystery why Ezemvelo Wildlife, which is mandated to conserve wildlife would euthanise healthy monkeys. Their supporters voiced their anger on social media.


V/O
The back yard where the monkey cages had been is now empty after Ezemvelo ordered Rowled to destroy them

In his court affidavit Jones stated that “in my 43 years as a conservation officer I have not seen such poor conditions in which animals were kept.”

However Ezemvelo had inspected the property only months before, in November 2020, and again in February 2021 and never CITED the conditions of the cages.

Steve
“The fact is that previously he had never shown any interest in the welfare of those animals. Now suddenly with all the negative publicity that KZN wildlife has had he’s now suddenly coming with a welfare based statement to the court. “


V/O
Karen Trendler says that the NSPCA is CONDUCTING its own investigation.

Karen
“And from the animal’s protection and the SPCA point of view there is an onus on the rescuer and the person who is running the rescue facility to be completely compliant in terms of cruelty and welfare standards, but those equally apply to the conservation officials, you still have to prevent suffering and cruelty. And that side needs to be looked at how those animals were handled when they were removed from the facility.”


Link
Tracy Rowles has secured rural land about 10 minutes away from here, to create a safe haven for the monkeys that she has dedicated her life to.”


V/O
Rowles claims that Ezemvelo WAS made aware of the land deal but it OPTED TO euthanise the vervets.

Umsizi’s lawyers were successful in bringing an interim interdict to stop Ezemvelo removing any more monkeys.

Tashya
“It just baffles me as to why there can be no working together. And why so many threats have been levelled against Umsizi Vervet Rescue. “



V/O
The legal matter is still continuing and it is hoped that this will force Ezemvelo to relook at adopting the 2008 Primates Norms and Standards to create a structure that can benefit all.

V/O
In the interim the fate of Rowles’ remaining monkeys hangs in the balance.

Tracy
“Those monkeys had been through so much before this even happened to be where they were , they didn’t deserve what they got.”



Monkey promos
(DARIO CONCERNED THAT I MENTION KZN WILDLIFE AUTHORITIES IN ALL PROMOS. I have adjusted them a bit?)

Promo 1
Tracy Rowles runs a vervet rehabilitation centre on the South Coast, without a permit from wildlife authorities – we investigate why healthy primates in her care were confiscated and euthanised.

Promo 2
Umsizi Umkomaas Rehabilitation Centre looks after vervet monkeys that have been abandoned or injured. We investigate the fate of monkeys that wildlife authorities confiscated from her premises.

Promo 3
Why would wildlife authorities whose mandate it is to conserve and protect wildlife confiscate 55 vervets from one of KZN South Coast’s monkey rehab centres?

Up sound Tashya “To date we have not heard of a refusal for those permits.” Masa ‘At the time that you did this you thought that this was the right body to apply for a permit with?” Tashya “It was the only body to apply for a permit. They will then write to you we would now refer the matter to the MEC and the MEC will grant you an exemption and we give you consent. But this did not happen here.” V/O Ezemvelo KZN WILDLIFE is governed by the Nature Conservation Ordinance 15 of 1974. Nearly 50 years ago, vervets were REGARDED as vermin and policy makers did not anticipate the need for regulating rehabilitation and rescue centres. Steve “The ordinance is an out dated document from 1974, Ordinance 15 and in that Ordinance it states that nobody is allowed to get a permit for a monkey or baboon from KZN Wildlife. V/O But the body can grant permits to circuses, zoos or research institutes that perform scientific tests on monkeys. Only the MEC can give Ezemvelo KZN WILDLIFE a concession to grant the permit. Tashya “Now we need to recognise that primates are sentient beings, they are not just property, they are not some group or species that needs to be rounded up and killed. So while we may have an idea for a protection of a domestic dog or cat , there is not the same for vervets.” V/O CARON To address the rights of vervets, the national SPCA’s Karen Trendler – together with other organisations – developed the Norms and Standards for the Management of Primates in 2008 – it was meant to replace the old ordinance. Karen (Caron not karen) “It would help from both a conservation permiting and welfare compliance point of view if that structure was in place. So that you had very set guidelines to what you can and can’t do.” V/O Trendler says it was up to Ezemvelo Wildlife to adopt the new guidelines. While it periodically inspected Umsizi, Ezemvelo confiscated the vervets in March this year because Umsizi still didn’t have a permit in terms of the old framework. Masa “So you are given 21 days to get rid of how many monkeys? Tracy “We are told to get rid of 117 monkeys in 21 days and there was no where for them to go there is no facility that would be able to take that amount of monkeys.” Up sound V/O As promised on the 29th of March Ezemvelo took about half of Umsizi’s 117 monkeys. The person heading up the confiscation WAS Dr Roy Jones, a senior district conservation manager at Ezemvelo. He did not tell Umsizi what he was going to do with the monkeys, but in his court affidavit he STATED that they had all been all euthanised. V/O Ezemvelo asked South Africa’s oldest rehabilitation Centre, CROW in Durban, to assist them catching the monkeys on the day. Clint Halkett-Siddall is Crow’s Operational Manager and says Ezemvelo told him the monkeys would be taken to Zululand. Masa “Now when you heard that these monkeys actually weren’t taken to Zululand and you found out what happened what were your thoughts?” (Cut out) Clive “We were obviously devastated as a team you know, we try to make sure that any animal is able to have a life back in the wild again.We actually took a decision with exco going forward that if Ezemvelo asked us for something like this we would say no.” V/O He says that CROW offered to house the Umsizi monkeys that Ezemvelo confiscated, but Ezemvelo turned down CROW’s offer on the day. Masa “So right now they could be here?” Clint “Any animals that could have been rehabilitated could have been here.We would have tried to get them to a point of release as soon as possible.” Masa “And instead?” Clint “Um ja.” V/O Ezemvelo has no rehabilitation centres of their own. In Jones’ affidavit he said that the monkeys “ could not be placed in any licensed rehabilitation centre.” Monkey Helpline disagrees. Steve If we had been asked by Ezemvelo at the time if we could have accomodated the monkeys from Tracy’s place the answer would have been emphatically yes. We have got the space and we would have built the cages and we would never have allowed them to be taken off into the fate that they were ultimately subjected to. Link “These are the Ezemvelo KZN Wildlife Head Offices in Pietermaritzburg. They are responsible for confiscating the vervet monkeys in March this year. We’ve requested an interview with them to get some answers, but they have declined the interview.” V/O We PHONED Dr Roy Jones who HAD headed up the operation. Roy “Roy Jones good day.” Masa “Good day Dr Jones this is Masa Kekana from CB.” Roy “Our CEO has already advised Carte Blanche that we are not in a position to discuss this at this stage.” Masa “But you were the ones who captured the monkeys?” Roy “No, not personally no.” Masa “Your organisation initiated this?” Roy “We initiated it, but we weren’t directly involved in the capture.” Masa “But you were there?” Roy “Correct” Masa “So you were involved and you are fully aware?” Roy “Yes, no, I am , I was just answering the question that you posed to me and I was just correcting it.” V/O EZEMVELO FACEBOOK TITLE It remains a mystery why Ezemvelo Wildlife, which is mandated to conserve wildlife would euthanise healthy monkeys. Their supporters voiced their anger on social media. V/O The back yard where the monkey cages had been is now empty after Ezemvelo ordered Rowled to destroy them In his court affidavit Jones stated that “in my 43 years as a conservation officer I have not seen such poor conditions in which animals were kept.” However Ezemvelo had inspected the property only months before, in November 2020, and again in February 2021 and never CITED the conditions of the cages. Steve “The fact is that previously he had never shown any interest in the welfare of those animals. Now suddenly with all the negative publicity that KZN wildlife has had he’s now suddenly coming with a welfare based statement to the court. “ V/O Karen Trendler says that the NSPCA is CONDUCTING its own investigation. Karen “And from the animal’s protection and the SPCA point of view there is an onus on the rescuer and the person who is running the rescue facility to be completely compliant in terms of cruelty and welfare standards, but those equally apply to the conservation officials, you still have to prevent suffering and cruelty. And that side needs to be looked at how those animals were handled when they were removed from the facility.” Link Tracy Rowles has secured rural land about 10 minutes away from here, to create a safe haven for the monkeys that she has dedicated her life to.” V/O Rowles claims that Ezemvelo WAS made aware of the land deal but it OPTED TO euthanise the vervets. Umsizi’s lawyers were successful in bringing an interim interdict to stop Ezemvelo removing any more monkeys. Tashya “It just baffles me as to why there can be no working together. And why so many threats have been levelled against Umsizi Vervet Rescue. “ V/O The legal matter is still continuing and it is hoped that this will force Ezemvelo to relook at adopting the 2008 Primates Norms and Standards to create a structure that can benefit all. V/O In the interim the fate of Rowles’ remaining monkeys hangs in the balance. Tracy “Those monkeys had been through so much before this even happened to be where they were , they didn’t deserve what they got.” Monkey promos (DARIO CONCERNED THAT I MENTION KZN WILDLIFE AUTHORITIES IN ALL PROMOS. I have adjusted them a bit?) Promo 1 Tracy Rowles runs a vervet rehabilitation centre on the South Coast, without a permit from wildlife authorities – we investigate why healthy primates in her care were confiscated and euthanised. Promo 2 Umsizi Umkomaas Rehabilitation Centre looks after vervet monkeys that have been abandoned or injured. We investigate the fate of monkeys that wildlife authorities confiscated from her premises. Promo 3 Why would wildlife authorities whose mandate it is to conserve and protect wildlife confiscate 55 vervets from one of KZN South Coast’s monkey rehab centres?

metadata.Further information: Vervet Monkey Proposal Tracy Rowls runs a rehab centre for vervet monkeys along the South Coast of KZN. It is called Umsizi Umkomaas Rehan Centre. For the past 16 years she had taken monkeys in and either acted as a foster parent for the young monkeys or helped monkeys that have been injured. There is an uneasy tension with monkeys along the KZN. Due to urbanization vervets have lost their habitat and live alongside humans. There is the one camp that see vervets as a nuisance and the others who believe we should try and live in harmony. Vervets have become habituated and are a nuisance when they come into homes and ransack kitchens. They will pull vegetables out of the ground and eat unripe fruit. At schools they also feed on the high calorie food that children leave behind. They can be aggressive. Some people actively dissuade vervets through srapying water on them or shooting them with pellet guns. The vet at Riverside says that almost 90% of monkeys that she sees has pellets lodged in their bodies when she X Rays them. Locals call Tracy the monkey lady and she is always there to help primates in distress. She lives in a suburban area and until recently had 119 monkeys on her property. Her neighbours were understandably unhappy about the amount of monkeys that she had. Tracy does not have a permit to house monkeys. Although she has applied to Ezemvelo several times they have not granted her a permit. In February Ezemvelo told her to find a place for the monkeys or they would confiscate them. Tracy has been for some time trying to find land to move the monkeys to. Her hope is to consolidate the monkeys into tribes and release them into the wild. (The jury is out as to whether monkeys can survive in the wild when they have been habituated. Whether without learning from adults they would know what food to eat.) Tracy did not find land and Ezemvelo came one Saturday morning and confiscated over 50 of her monkeys. CROW, another wild life rehab centre helped them catch the monkeys. What no-one knew was that Ezemvelo had no intention of releasing these monkeys into the wild and they were driven in a truck and euthenised. On inspection some of the cages that Tracy had kept the monkeys in were in a bad state. She obviously lacks the funds to look after them and the cages had rusty nails sticking out of the wood. The SPCA was also there to monitor the capture of the monkeys and they too did not know that the monkeys would be killed. Tracy has taken out a court order against Ezemvelo taking any more monkeys and the case will be heard on the 19th of May. Vervets are not endangered. But what line does one draw? Rehabbing vervets is very expensive and time consuming and academics argue that the money used to help monkeys could be better spent on other conservation initiatives. Interviews Tracy Rowles - Monkey Rehab. Had 119 monkeys on her property. Umkomaas Umsizi Rehab Centre. Ezemvelo removed 50 and killed them. She is looking for land and it looks like she is moving her monkeys there.No permission to rehab monkeys. Steve Smith and Carol Booth run Monkey Helpline lots of visuals very passionate about monkeys have a sanctuary in Camperdown. They do have permission to rehab monkeys. Adrian neighbour to Steve and Carol and complained to us about monkeys.Steve and Carol say no monkeys at home now all at Camperdown. Neighbour represents people who don’t like the vervets. CROW Rehab. They have permission to rehab monkeys and went to help Ezemvelo capture the monkeys. They say they did not know that they would be euthanised. They do however have to believe in rehab to keep their jobs. Clint. Ezemvelo - don’t think they will grant us an interview but we will be able to get them in court on the 19th of May. We are applying to film court proceedings. Tony is helping me. Harriet Thatcher or Colleen Downs from UKZN have done research/studies on vervet and humans. Kerry from Riverside vet - has seen many more animals with pellet gun bullets. Tash lawyer and animal lover that is helping Tracey fight for rights of monkeys. Talks about cruelty of Ezemvelo. Need a conservation expert.
